history.dynasty: Thanjavur Maratha, c. 1760s, during ruler Pratap Singh Bhonsle (Wikipedia); tradition says the idol was brought from Kanchipuram by the Nayaks to protect it from invaders
history.period: 18th century (present structure c. 1760s); kumbhabhishekams in 1992, 2004 and 2017
history.summary: A DISTINCT Thanjavur temple - not a CSV error. It is different from the famous Kamakshi Amman Temple of Kanchipuram (seq 2225): the presiding deity is a small swayambhu gold ('bangaru') idol of Kamakshi in a seated posture, believed to have been shifted from Kanchipuram by the Nayaks and disguised with punugu (civet secretion), which still gives the goddess's face its black colour. Shyama Sastri, one of the Trinity of Carnatic music, was born in the family that served as this temple's priests. Rajagopuram, front mandapa and vimana; temple stands on West Main Street in Thanjavur city. CSV town Thanjavur is correct.

name: Kamakshi Amman Temple
town_description: Thanjavur (Tanjore) is the historic Chola capital on the south bank of the Cauvery in Thanjavur district. The Bangaru Kamakshi temple stands on West Main Street in the old city, a short distance from Thanjavur Junction railway station.

travel.airport: Tiruchirappalli International Airport, about 60 km away.
travel.road: In Thanjavur city on West Main Street; city buses and autos from the railway station.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Fridays are special for the goddess.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-12:00 PM and 4:00 PM-9:00 PM (verify: one listing shows morning session only, 6:00 AM-12:00 PM). No entry fee.
